priority_definition.P1: Correctness boundary repair before optimization; no frequency or catastrophic-severity claim.

scope: Source trace and pinned-engine headless/component/accepted-session witnesses, no rendered or native performance qualification.

findings.title: Graphics calibration reset intent escapes the Settings transaction
findings.tracking_status: Additional transaction defect; related to, but distinct from, F04-F08 calibration identity/policy findings.
findings.observation: Actual Settings methods leave calibration reset pending after Revert. A later successful volume-only Keep in the same production-path instance deletes saved/live calibration. Restore at already-recommended values leaves reset pending but Keep/Revert disabled. The forced display-expiry case repeats the stale intent; close/destroy/reopen is a negative control.
findings.impact: Canceled graphics intent can be committed by an unrelated setting; a reset-only intent cannot be committed when dictionary values are unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Represent calibration reset as transaction state, include it in dirty/Keep/Revert logic, and specify how display-only expiry relates to remaining graphics edits.
findings.verification_plan: Restore/Revert/unrelated Keep; identical-value Restore; Restore/Keep; failed save; display-only expiry; expiry with other graphics edits; close/destroy/reopen.
findings.limits: Method-driven headless UI with synthetic recommendations/calibration, fallback fonts and a constant-only preferences stub. No timed UI interaction, physical renderer or immediate remeasurement measured.

findings.title: Angle target is discontinuous at the heading cutoff, with a representation-dependent exact half-turn tie
findings.tracking_status: New reproduced controller boundary cases; one finding with two explicitly separated subcases.
findings.observation: Paired attitudes about 2e-8 rad apart across the 0.2 horizontal-nose cutoff produce a 1.2595647167 rad/s raw roll-target difference at bank 0.3 rad, 1.1044559836 rad/s after filtering and 0.4011384132 N m requested-torque difference. Both pitch signs reproduce; zero bank is a control. Exact q=[0,1,0,0] and -q produce opposite +/-6.981317008 rad/s targets; nearby nonzero scalar sign pairs agree.
findings.impact: An artificial heading switch makes finite controller outputs jump for arbitrarily close admitted body attitudes. The exact half-turn tie also depends on quaternion representation.
findings.recommendation: Choose a locally continuous near-vertical reference/tilt policy with explicit singular-attitude handling. Define a deterministic vector-part tie at exact half-turn. Moving the threshold or translating the branch to native code does not repair the law.
findings.verification_plan: Boundary sweeps for bank/yaw/pitch signs; equivalent quaternion signs; mode-entry/reset; stock-powertrain closed-loop recovery, saturation and replay.
findings.limits: Paired independently initialized component samples, identical zero histories/rates and a laboratory static actuator-map/allocator, supply voltage zero. No motor-lag dynamics advanced. Requested torque is not actual flight torque; no consecutive-tick maneuver, crash or ordinary half-turn occurrence established. No globally continuous shortest-turn rule exists at every half-turn.

findings.title: Airship public verifier returns exact and ok after detecting a changed solver fingerprint
findings.tracking_status: New public-verifier policy counterexample; the visible solver_changed flag and existing documentation are acknowledged.
findings.observation: A valid 24-row airship recording, after a 12-tick checkpoint at 240 Hz, passes same-source verify. A comment appended to the copied fixture math source changes the fingerprint in a fresh process; unchanged recording bytes still yield complete/identity_match/exact/ok true and solver_changed true.
findings.impact: The exact result does not enforce the verifier comment's same-solver contract and differs from multirotor behavior. Callers that use exact/ok alone can overstate certification.
findings.recommendation: Require a known unchanged solver before exact=true, or explicitly separate trajectory-byte comparison from exact replay across APIs, CLI and documentation.
findings.verification_plan: Same-source, comment-only source change, changed numerical implementation, changed session identity and incomplete recording; verify CLI report/exit semantics.
findings.limits: Public verifier executed, CLI source-traced only. The source change is a comment in a disposable dependency closure, not changed physics or release solver qualification. Flag remains visible and the existing guide already says to check it.

findings.title: Airship replay omits semantic checks of row ticks and footer time bounds
findings.tracking_status: Reproduced at the parsed-record component seam; public-inspector omission is source-supported, not exercised with a malformed file.
findings.observation: Copies of a legitimate parsed record with duplicate ticks, a 100-tick gap, reordered first two labels or footer bounds -10/-20 all yield exact/ok from the actual replay component. The inspector checks chains, arrays and counts but not those semantic timeline invariants.
findings.impact: A state-row byte match can certify a different tick labeling/timeline. Exported tick/time metadata may not describe the replayed sequence.
findings.recommendation: Validate consecutive row ticks against checkpoint.tick + replay tick, and footer checkpoint/final bounds before stepping; retain existing packet integrity and terminal-crash checks.
findings.verification_plan: Correctly checksummed malformed public-file cases; valid nonzero checkpoints; supported zero/one-row cases; terminal crash and incomplete records. Footer first_tick denotes the checkpoint boundary, not first recorded row.
findings.limits: No recording bytes altered or malformed file submitted. Stock writer already requires consecutive ticks and ordinary bit corruption is rejected. Airship replay time reset is intentional under time-invariant wind, not a separate defect.

findings.title: Unavailable replay identity can compare equal to another unavailable identity
findings.tracking_status: Conditional source finding; no release-package failure reproduced.
findings.observation: The shared helper may return kind unavailable, sha256 unavailable-export. Airship/multirotor writers store it without requiring availability, and verifier SHA-only comparisons make two sentinel values set solver_changed=false. Otherwise matching state checks can then allow exact certification.
findings.impact: Unknown solver identity is treated as known equality under an otherwise-runnable package-identity failure.
findings.recommendation: Make identity availability explicit and required for exact certification; compare kind/version and digest as appropriate. Permit diagnostic recording separately if desired.
findings.verification_plan: Isolated actual release fixtures with valid, absent or invalid receipt; recorded/current unavailable identity; ordinary same-source and candidate modes.
findings.limits: Source trace only. Normal shipped packages are not claimed to lack receipts. No altered package execution or cross-package trajectory experiment. Mac startup can retain an unavailable receipt without globally blocking the experimental session paths; reachability depends on the rest of the package remaining runnable.

findings.title: Connected input polls scan 128 buttons in the reviewed unbound-AUX path
findings.area: CPU / input callback and allocation work
findings.tracking_status: Additional operation-count candidate; distinct from the already optimized binding resolver.
findings.observation: Actual RCInput.poll with valid profile, fake readers, an injected synthetic-gamepad verifier and unbound AUX performs 30,720 button and 2,400 axis callbacks over 240 direct polls, both active and integrate=false. No input/profile errors; armed state preserved.
findings.impact: Full button-history collection is repeated even where standard-gamepad readiness does not require a release. Its share of complete session cost remains unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Attribute actual workload cost; determine per-profile evidence needs and investigate eligible narrower queries or one same-tick snapshot. A batch native boundary is conditional on measured dispatch/data movement cost.
findings.verification_plan: Raw-radio/event evidence, focus/hotplug/source generation, non-finite axes, holds/rate throttle/AUX and current verified-gamepad policy; complete input/session timing before any native port.
findings.limits: Counts only, no physical device, menu, USB traffic, latency, timing or FPS. Per-second count only applies if 240 polls happen in that wall second. Other bindings may add reads and profiles may early-return. Do not decimate required input evidence to frame cadence.

findings.title: Plant instance scale changes the world wave displacement applied in local space
findings.tracking_status: Source plus scalar/Transform3D witness; no rendered artifact claimed.
findings.observation: The lily shader adds the world-coordinate analytic wave height to local VERTEX.y. Generated lily-pad scales are approximately 0.28-0.47 and flowers use 1.25. At matched phase/fade, extra world displacement is s*h and the discrepancy is (s-1)*h. Actual generated sample calculations give about -6.35 mm for one pad and -0.819 mm for one flower.
findings.impact: Accepted instance size changes wave-following amplitude independently of the shared water-wave definition.
findings.recommendation: Apply the displacement in world space or transform the vector correctly to local space, preserving phase/base offsets and all existing model-coordinate uses. Validate bounds from an explicit envelope.
findings.verification_plan: Multiple scales, shore/interior and cycle samples; actual shader/rendered comparison of motion, normals, fade and bounds at target resolutions/renderers.
findings.limits: No shader or mesh-vertex execution, GPU timing, rendered gap or culling failure. Uses unchanged generated placements and local-origin Transform3D math. Water UV2/interpolation and plant instance fade may differ, so (s-1)h isolates scale rather than the entire rendered separation.

findings.title: CG-only terrain early-outs skip an overlapping multirotor on an admitted custom ramp
findings.tracking_status: Concrete component and accepted-session reproduction of a previously tracked unsafe-bound concern, not a newly discovered concern.
findings.observation: With shipped quad/default field and a valid in-memory ramp height 1.2 m/approach 0.1 m, an intentionally overlapping research air start has 0.7000000001 m CG clearance, 0.2777584124 m contact-point penetration and two rotor-disc witnesses. Strict/graded sessions prepare, resume and accept one tick while returned contact force is zero, crash/fault absent, substeps=1 and prop health unchanged. The separate 0.59 m component control produces force, prop strike and graded damage; the 0.70 m component case does not.
findings.impact: The optimized exclusion is not conservative across the admitted terrain footprint; changing native implementation or thresholds alone cannot certify contact correctness.
findings.recommendation: Use a conservative whole-footprint and swept-motion terrain upper bound, with prepared local/cell bounds or a coarse global fallback, or refuse unsupported geometry explicitly.
findings.verification_plan: Retain custom overlap and nearby-clearance controls and add a flat-ground control; stock/custom terrain, orientation/rotor geometry, natural approach trajectories, strict/graded contact, substeps and exact accepted history; measure complete-tick cost after repair.
findings.limits: Intentional overlap/research start, not a naturally flown or stock-course crash. Session depth uses the memoized plant sampler; component control uses direct track sampling. No scenery obstacle inventory. Rotor initialization/coast behavior is preserved. No full physical validation or performance saving measured.

findings.title: Admitted shore fade differs between clamped water material and plant/physical consumers
findings.tracking_status: Additional valid-custom-data mismatch; default 5.5 m fade unaffected.
findings.observation: Actual Loader.validate accepts shore_fade_m=50; water-material source clamps to 12 while plants/physical surface use 50. At the same modeled distance of 6 m, smoothstep factors are 0.5 and 0.039744.
findings.impact: One admitted lake definition produces incompatible wave envelopes across consumers.
findings.recommendation: Share a single range/normalization contract, or explicitly reject unsupported renderer parameters at admission; align shader inspector hints.
findings.verification_plan: Public loader/material paths at minimum/default/12/just-over-12/50 m, matched spatial/time samples and actual rendered shore/contact cue inspection.
findings.limits: Actual loader plus scalar model of source clamp, not water-material/shader execution or a measured GPU/pixel result. Default unaffected; custom CLI route has default-field/scenery/amplitude gates.

findings.title: Valid custom wave periods violate 1024-second shader-clock continuity
findings.tracking_status: Additional admitted-custom-period case; default 2/4-second periods satisfy the clock contract.
findings.observation: The actual loader accepts a 3 s period while ShaderClock wraps at 1024 s. 1024/3 is not integral, leaving a 2pi/3 phase mismatch. At an actual generated point, selected samples at 1023.999/1024 s give physical down-height delta +0.00003390565 m versus source-modeled wrapped shader delta -0.0265582651 m.
findings.impact: Visible wave phase can jump and differ from continuous physical water height at a wrap for admitted custom periods.
findings.recommendation: Constrain admitted periods explicitly or derive bounded per-wave phases from authoritative float64 time; preserve authored frequency, pause/reset and water/plant ownership.
findings.verification_plan: Supported period classes/defaults/3 s at wraps, pause/resume/reset/origin, long-session rendered continuity and uniform-submission cost if phase moves to CPU.
findings.limits: Real loader, physical sampler and ShaderClock.value; CPU-modeled shader equation at selected analytic times. No observed adjacent 240 Hz ticks, shader execution or rendered 17-minute flight. No claimed default-lake failure.
